page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg6.6xlarge is an x86_64 server instance running under KVM virtualization, featuring a 3.1 GHz Intel Xeon 8269CY processor. The system is equipped with 12 physical cores and 24 dedicated vCPUs via symmetric multithreading, supported by 35 MB of shared L3 cache and per-core L1 and L2 caches. It provides 96 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio with 4.0 GB of memory per core. The instance includes an 8 Gbps baseline network throughput interface. Hardware accelerators such as discrete GPUs are not included, and no local disk storage is bundled, requiring the attachment of remote block storage for persistence.

Instruction set support includes AVX, AVX-512F, and AVX-512 VNNI for vectorized arithmetic and vector neural network operations, as well as hardware-accelerated AES cryptography. Across synthetic tests, the instance records middle-tier scores relative to its peer group, demonstrating a PassMark CPU score of 23,637.6 and a multi-core stress-ng metric of 23,015.19. Memory benchmarks show large-block read bandwidth reaching 109.43 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 48.03 GB/sec. Application testing demonstrates 22.14 million operations per second in Redis SET operations and a static web serving rate of 17.13 GB/sec, while CPU-based inference executes at 78.25 tokens per second for small 135M parameter models.

Qualitative cost efficiency is centered around the instance's high base clock speed combined with a balanced memory allocation, avoiding cost overhead associated with integrated local NVMe storage or specialized GPU accelerators. The primary operational tradeoff is total dependency on network-attached storage for disk operations, which must share host I/O paths alongside runtime network activities. This profile aligns directly with compute-heavy general workloads, software compilation pipelines, in-memory caching clusters, static web delivery platforms, and enterprise business backend systems.
